title_en: China Biodiversity Conservation and Green Development Foundation v. [Appellee] — appeal against ruling of non-acceptance by Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region High People's Court
ruling_gist_en: To determine whether a social organization falls within the scope of 'an organization specially engaged in environmental protection public welfare activities' as stipulated in Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law, it shall comprehensively consider whether the organization's mission and business scope include safeguarding the environmental public interest, whether it actually engages in environmental protection public welfare activities, and whether the environmental public interest it safeguards is related to its mission and business scope. Whether an organization's mission and business scope include safeguarding the environmental public interest shall be determined based on its substance rather than merely on the literal expression.
keywords_en: Civil; Environmental pollution public interest litigation; Retrial; Supreme People's Court; Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region; Social organization; Environmental Protection Law; Civil Procedure Law; Whether a social organization is an organization specially engaged in environmental protection public welfare activities; Whether the organizational purpose and business scope include safeguarding the environmental public interest; Reversal of judgment; Environmental pollution; Tengger Desert pollution; Social organization filing public interest litigation; Clarify the criteria for determining specially engaged in environmental protection public welfare activities; Application for retrial
full_text_en:
China Biodiversity Conservation and Green Development Foundation v. The Ruling of the High People's Court of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region on Refusal to Accept the Case

[Ruling Summary]

In determining whether a social organization is an organization "specially engaged in environmental protection public interest activities" as defined in Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law, a comprehensive assessment shall be made of whether the organization's purpose and scope of business include the maintenance of environmental public interests, whether it actually engages in environmental protection public interest activities, and whether the environmental public interest it seeks to protect is related to its purpose and scope of business. Whether the organization's purpose and scope of business include the maintenance of environmental public interests shall be determined based on its substance rather than merely on its literal wording.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2016) Zui Gao Fa Min Zai No. 51

Retrial Applicant (First Instance Plaintiff, Second Instance Appellant): China Biodiversity Conservation and Green Development Foundation. Address: No. 98, Xigexinli, Yongdingmenwai, Dongcheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Hu Deping, Chairman of the Foundation.

Agents ad litem: Wang Haijun, lawyer of Beijing Deheheng Law Firm.

Agents ad litem: Wang Xiao, lawyer of Beijing Deheheng Law Firm.

The retrial applicant, China Biodiversity Conservation and Green Development Foundation (hereinafter referred to as the Green Development Foundation), dissatisfied with the Civil Ruling (2015) Ning Min Gong Li Zhong Zi No. 1 of the High People's Court of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region in a case of environmental pollution public interest litigation against Zhongwei Meiliyuan Water Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Meiliyuan Company), applied to this Court for retrial. After this Court decided to bring the case up for retrial, a collegial panel was formed in accordance with the law to conduct the trial. The trial has now been concluded.

The Green Development Foundation filed a lawsuit with the Intermediate People's Court of Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, alleging: Meiliyuan Company had long been discharging production wastewater in excess of standards in violation of regulations, causing serious pollution to the Tengger Desert. After the relevant authorities ordered rectification, the rectification progress was slow, and as of the time of filing the lawsuit, the rectification had not been completed. The lawsuit requested the court to order Meiliyuan Company to: (1) cease the illegal behavior of polluting the environment; (2) eliminate the dangers caused by environmental pollution; (3) restore the ecological environment or establish a special fund for desert environmental restoration and entrust a qualified third party to carry out the restoration; (4) for the claims in items (2) and (3), have the court organize the plaintiff, technical experts, legal experts, people's congress deputies, and CPPCC members to jointly accept the results; (5) compensate for ecological function losses before environmental restoration; (6) publicly apologize in national media; (7) bear reasonable expenses such as appraisal fees, travel expenses, and lawyer fees incurred by the Green Development Foundation; (8) bear the litigation costs of this case.

The court of first instance held: Although the purpose and scope of business of the Green Development Foundation are to maintain social public interests, its articles of association do not specify that the Foundation also meets the requirement of "engaging in environmental protection public interest activities" as stipulated in Article 4 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Civil Public Interest Lawsuits (hereinafter referred to as the Environmental Public Interest Litigation Judicial Interpretation), and the scope of business determined in the Foundation's registration certificate does not include engaging in environmental protection business. Therefore, the Green Development Foundation cannot be recognized as a social organization "specially engaged in environmental protection public interest activities" as provided in Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Environmental Protection Law). Pursuant to Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law, Article 4 of the Environmental Public Interest Litigation Judicial Interpretation, and Article 123 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Civil Procedure Law), the court of first instance ruled to reject the lawsuit filed by the Green Development Foundation.

The Green Development Foundation, dissatisfied with the ruling of the first instance, appealed to the High People's Court of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, arguing: The court of first instance failed to correctly understand the concepts of "environment" and "environmental protection," thus erroneously concluding that the purpose and scope of business of the Green Development Foundation did not include "engaging in environmental protection public interest activities." The appeal requested: (1) to overturn the ruling of the first instance; (2) to accept the lawsuit filed by the Green Development Foundation in accordance with the law.

The court of second instance held: The appeal of the Green Development Foundation did not conform to the provisions of Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law and Articles 4 and 5 of the Environmental Public Interest Litigation Judicial Interpretation, and the grounds of appeal were untenable. Pursuant to Paragraph 1, Item 1 of Article 170, Article 171, and Article 175 of the Civil Procedure Law, the court of second instance ruled to dismiss the appeal of the Green Development Foundation and uphold the ruling of the first instance.

The Green Development Foundation, dissatisfied with the ruling of the second instance, applied to this Court for retrial, arguing: (1) The ruling of the second instance did not state the facts and reasons, nor did it provide a legal analysis of the appellate arguments, simply concluding that the Green Development Foundation's grounds of appeal did not conform to the provisions of Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law and Articles 4 and 5 of the Environmental Public Interest Litigation Judicial Interpretation. This did not meet the content requirements for a civil ruling and was not conducive to the effective implementation of the environmental civil public interest litigation system. (2) The ruling of the first instance failed to correctly understand the concepts of "environment" and "environmental protection," erroneously concluding that the purpose and scope of business of the Green Development Foundation did not include "engaging in environmental protection public interest activities." Expressions in the Green Development Foundation's articles of association such as "biodiversity conservation," "green development cause," "ecological civilization construction," "harmony between man and nature," and "building a beautiful homeland for mankind" all fall within the scope of environmental protection. The first instance ruling, solely on the grounds that there was no literal wording of "environmental protection public interest activities," concluded that the Green Development Foundation had not engaged in environmental protection public interest activities. This constitutes a mechanical understanding of legal provisions and should be corrected. (3) The Green Development Foundation's actual engagement in environmental protection public interest activities also confirms the purpose and scope of business of "environmental protection public interest activities" as set out in its articles of association. Article 4 of the Environmental Public Interest Litigation Judicial Interpretation relaxes the review standards for social organizations specializing in environmental protection public interest activities, reflecting the judicial orientation of encouraging social organizations to initiate environmental civil public interest lawsuits in accordance with the law. Since its establishment, the Green Development Foundation has been consistently engaged in public interest activities related to environmental protection. The ruling of the second instance incorrectly interpreted the above provisions of the Environmental Public Interest Litigation Judicial Interpretation, constituting an error in the application of law. The retrial application requested: (1) to overturn the rulings of the first and second instances; (2) to accept the lawsuit filed by the Green Development Foundation in accordance with the law.

This Court finds: During the first instance, the Green Development Foundation submitted a foundation legal person registration certificate, showing that it is a foundation legal person registered with the Ministry of Civil Affairs of the People's Republic of China; submitted certification materials for annual inspections for the years 2009 to 2013, showing that it had passed annual inspections for five consecutive years; submitted a statement of no violations, declaring that it had not received any administrative or criminal penalties for violating laws and regulations in the course of its business activities within the past five years. During the second instance, the Green Development Foundation submitted photographs of activities such as "Ecological Education Campus Tour," "Environmental Public Interest Litigation Case Seminar," "China Nature Reserve Sustainable Development Management Training Class," "Sino-US Air Purification Seminar," and "Trip to Yajiang to Rescue the Five-leaf Maple," showing that it had organized or participated in environmental protection public interest activities. During the retrial, the Green Development Foundation submitted an introduction to its historical evolution, showing that its predecessor was the China Milu Foundation established in 1985, which had long been engaged in the protection and breeding of milu deer populations; submitted seven case acceptance notices, including (2015) Hai Zhong Fa Huan Min Chu Zi No. 1 from the Intermediate People's Court of Haikou City, Hainan Province, and (2015) Qing Hai Fa Hai Shi Chu Zi No. 117 from the Qingdao Maritime Court, showing that multiple environmental civil public interest lawsuits it had filed had been accepted; submitted certification materials for the annual inspection for 2014, showing that it had passed the annual inspection for 2014.

This Court holds: This case is an environmental pollution public interest lawsuit filed by a social organization. The retrial applicant, the Green Development Foundation, believes that the courts of first and second instance erred in law by concluding that it is not a social organization "engaged in environmental protection public interest activities" and thus ruling not to accept its lawsuit. Therefore, this case should focus on whether the Green Development Foundation is a social organization specially engaged in environmental protection public interest activities.

To ensure orderly public participation in environmental governance, establish and remedy public environmental rights and interests, and pursue the legal liability of tortfeasors in accordance with the law, Article 55 of the Civil Procedure Law establishes the environmental civil public interest litigation system, clearly stating that organs and relevant organizations as provided by law may initiate environmental public interest lawsuits. Because environmental public interests are inclusive and shared, and there are no specific legally directly interested parties, it is necessary to encourage, guide, and regulate social organizations to initiate environmental public interest lawsuits in accordance with the law, in order to fully utilize the functions of environmental public interest litigation. Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law provides: "For acts that pollute the environment, destroy ecology, and harm social public interests, social organizations that meet the following conditions may initiate lawsuits in a people's court: (1) They are lawfully registered with the civil affairs department of a people's government at or above the level of a city divided into districts; (2) They have been specially engaged in environmental protection public interest activities for five consecutive years or more and have no record of violations. If a social organization that meets the conditions specified in the preceding paragraph initiates a lawsuit in a people's court, the people's court shall accept it in accordance with the law." Article 4 of the Environmental Public Interest Litigation Judicial Interpretation further clarifies the criteria for determining whether a social organization is "specially engaged in environmental protection public interest activities," providing that "if the purpose and main scope of business determined in the articles of association of a social organization are to maintain social public interests and it engages in environmental protection public interest activities, it may be recognized as an organization 'specially engaged in environmental protection public interest activities' as provided in Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law. The social public interests involved in the lawsuit initiated by the social organization shall be related to its purpose and scope of business." Therefore, whether the Green Development Foundation in this case may be recognized as a social organization "specially engaged in environmental protection public interest activities" for the purpose of initiating this lawsuit should be examined from three aspects: whether its purpose and scope of business include the maintenance of environmental public interests, whether it actually engages in environmental protection public interest activities, and whether the environmental public interest it seeks to protect is related to its purpose and scope of business.

I. Whether the purpose and scope of business stipulated in the articles of association of the Green Development Foundation include the maintenance of environmental public interests

The common interests enjoyed by the public in living and developing in a healthy, comfortable, and beautiful environment take various forms. Whether the purpose and scope of business of a social organization include the maintenance of environmental public interests shall be determined based on its substance rather than merely on its literal wording. Even if the articles of association of a social organization do not explicitly mention the maintenance of environmental public interests, if its work content falls within the scope of protecting various natural factors, whether natural or artificially modified, that affect human survival and development, including the protection of environmental elements such as the atmosphere, water, oceans, land, mineral deposits, forests, grasslands, wetlands, wildlife, natural relics, cultural relics, nature reserves, scenic spots, cities, and villages, and their ecosystems, it shall be deemed that the purpose and scope of business include the maintenance of environmental public interests.

The United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity, signed by China in 1992, states that biological diversity means the variability among living organisms from all sources including, inter alia, terrestrial, marine and other aquatic ecosystems and the ecological complexes of which they are part; this includes diversity within species, between species and of ecosystems. Article 30 of the Environmental Protection Law provides: "In the development and utilization of natural resources, development shall be rational, biodiversity shall be protected, ecological security shall be ensured, and plans for ecological protection and restoration and governance shall be formulated and implemented in accordance with the law. When introducing alien species and researching, developing, and utilizing biotechnology, measures shall be taken to prevent damage to biodiversity." It is evident that biodiversity conservation is an important part of environmental protection and also an important component of maintaining environmental public interests.

The articles of association of the Green Development Foundation clearly stipulate that its purpose is "to extensively mobilize the whole society to care about and support the cause of biodiversity conservation and green development, protect national strategic resources, promote ecological civilization construction and harmony between man and nature, and build a beautiful homeland for mankind," which conforms to the requirements of the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity and the Environmental Protection Law on biodiversity conservation. Furthermore, the content of "promoting ecological civilization construction," "harmony between man and nature," and "building a beautiful homeland for mankind" aligns with the concept of green development, is closely related to environmental protection, and falls within the category of maintaining environmental public interests. Therefore, it should be determined that the purpose and scope of business of the Green Development Foundation include the maintenance of environmental public interests.

II. Whether the Green Development Foundation actually engages in environmental protection public interest activities

Environmental protection public interest activities include not only direct behaviors that improve the ecological environment, such as afforestation, protection of endangered species, energy conservation and emission reduction, and environmental restoration, but also activities related to environmental protection, such as publicity and education, research and training, academic exchanges, legal aid, and public interest litigation, which are conducive to improving the environmental governance system, enhancing environmental governance capacity, and promoting broad consensus on environmental protection in society. The relevant evidence materials submitted by the Green Development Foundation during the first instance, second instance, and retrial, including historical evolution, photographs of public interest activities, and notices of acceptance of environmental public interest lawsuits, although not cross-examined, are sufficient at the case acceptance review stage to show that the Green Development Foundation has long been actually engaged in environmental protection activities since its establishment in 1985, including holding environmental protection seminars, organizing ecological surveys, conducting environmental protection publicity and education, and initiating environmental civil public interest lawsuits, which complies with the provisions of the Environmental Protection Law and the Environmental Public Interest Litigation Judicial Interpretation. At the same time, the above evidence also proves that the Green Development Foundation has been engaged in environmental protection public interest activities for more than five years, meeting the requirement under Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law that a social organization should have been engaged in environmental protection public interest activities for five years or more.

III. Whether the social public interests involved in this case are related to the purpose and scope of business of the Green Development Foundation

Pursuant to Article 4 of the Environmental Public Interest Litigation Judicial Interpretation, the environmental public interest involved in a public interest lawsuit initiated by a social organization shall have a certain connection with the purpose and scope of business of the social organization. This provision is intended to ensure that the environmental public interest protection matters brought by the social organization correspond to or are related to its purpose and scope of business, so as to ensure that the social organization has the corresponding litigation capacity. Therefore, even if the matter brought by the social organization does not correspond to its purpose and scope of business, if it has a certain connection with the environmental elements or ecosystems it protects, the qualification of the social organization as a litigant should still be recognized based on the criterion of relevance. The environmental public interest lawsuit in this case is brought against the pollution of the Tengger Desert. The complex and fragile desert ecosystem formed by the interaction of desert biological communities and their environment requires more careful utilization and protection by humans. The Green Development Foundation alleged that Meiliyuan Company had long been discharging wastewater in excess of standards in violation of regulations, seriously damaging the already fragile ecosystem of the Tengger Desert. The protection of the environmental public interest involved falls within the purpose and scope of business of the Green Development Foundation.

Furthermore, the foundation legal person registration certificate submitted by the Green Development Foundation shows that it is a foundation legal person registered with the Ministry of Civil Affairs of the People's Republic of China. The certification materials for annual inspections from 2010 to 2014 submitted by the Green Development Foundation show that it had passed annual inspections for the five years prior to initiating this public interest lawsuit. The Green Development Foundation also submitted a statement of no violations as required by Article 5 of the Environmental Public Interest Litigation Judicial Interpretation, declaring that it had not received any administrative or criminal penalties for violating laws and regulations in the course of its business activities within the past five years. Accordingly, the Green Development Foundation also meets the other requirements for social organizations to initiate environmental civil public interest lawsuits under Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law and Articles 2, 3, and 5 of the Environmental Public Interest Litigation Judicial Interpretation, and has the standing to initiate environmental civil public interest lawsuits.

In conclusion, the rulings of the first and second instances in this case, which found that the Green Development Foundation lacked the standing to initiate an environmental civil public interest lawsuit, resulted from an incorrect understanding of the Environmental Protection Law, the Environmental Public Interest Litigation Judicial Interpretation, and the connotation of environmental protection. The application of law was indeed erroneous and should be corrected. The retrial application of the Green Development Foundation is meritorious, and this Court supports it. Pursuant to Article 58 of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, Paragraph 1 of Article 207 and Paragraph 1, Item 2 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Environmental Civil Public Interest Lawsuits, and Paragraph 2 of Article 407 and Article 332 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ruled as follows:

1. The Civil Ruling (2015) Ning Min Gong Li Zhong Zi No. 1 of the High People's Court of Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region and the Civil Ruling (2015) Wei Min Gong Li Zi No. 1 of the Intermediate People's Court of Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, are hereby reversed;

2. This case shall be accepted by the Intermediate People's Court of Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region.

This ruling is a final ruling.

Presiding Judge: Liu Xiaofei
Acting Judge: Wu Kaimin
Acting Judge: Ye Yang

January 28, 2016

Clerk: Wei Ran

[Introduction of Presiding Judge]

Liu Xiaofei, Senior Judge, born in 1976, Doctor of Laws, appointed as a Judge of the Supreme People's Court in 2015.
